label: PF Backlog 651
title: Backlog execution trail: ordered stage ledger + tests/usage/cost report + completion guard

brief.problem: Backlog execution is ad hoc: no single ordered trail of gates/tests/decisions/PR/usage/cost per item.
brief.what_adds: A registered append-only execution-trail store, a show/finalize CLI, automatic writes from the gate tools, and a completion gate.
brief.why_now: EDP-10/1480 showed the process is only as good as the visible trail; every session/LLM must follow it.
brief.success: Every completion has an ordered trail with tests/results/time/PR/usage and a final next-item table; missing stages fail precheck.

objective: Give every backlog item one ordered, append-only execution trail from Gate 0 to completion, written automatically by the gate tools, with a show CLI (gates, tests, usage, final table, next item) and a completion gate that fails missing/out-of-order stages.
acceptance_criteria: A registered store engineering/trails/<ITEM>.json (owner core/execution_trail.py) records append-only events {seq, at, stage, actor, status, summary, refs, tests, usage, duration_ms} for planning, gate0, design_review, gate1, implementation, code_review, diff_review, gate2, tests, precheck, pr, merge, delivery, completion.

python -m core.execution_trail show --item <ID> renders the ordered trail, the Gate 1.5/2.5 decision tables + recommendations (from the review evidence), the tests table (command/result/duration), usage totals (input/output/cached tokens; 'not captured' when unavailable), and the final completion table with PR/merge, total time, next backlog item.

The gate tools write the trail automatically: gate0_check, architect_review (design/diff + provider usage), gate_decide, precheck (tests/precheck timings), core.backlog.set_delivery and set_status(completed); no manual record is needed for a normal item.

scripts/dev/execution_trail_check.py (precheck fast) fails a completion in the diff when required stages are missing or out of order, or when a DEFERRED finding has no follow-up item; the check is self-tested and wired into precheck + ci-cd-gates.
out_of_scope: Fabricating coding-session token counts/cost (only captured sources are recorded).
Retroactively backfilling every legacy item (completion gate applies to items in the diff).
Changing the gate order or review framework.
approach: Add core/execution_trail.py (registered store engineering/trails/<ID>.json, append-only events, lock, record/show/finalize/check helpers) and scripts/dev/execution_trail_check.py. Wire gate0_check, architect_review (design/diff + provider usage), gate_decisions (gate1/2), precheck (tests/precheck timings), core.backlog.set_delivery and set_status(completed). show renders the ordered stages, the Gate 1.5/2.5 tables via architect_review.render_gate_view, the tests table, usage totals and the final completion/next-item table. The completion gate requires gate0/design_review/gate1/diff_review/gate2/tests in order and a follow-up item for DEFERRED findings.

prior_decisions: Gate 0/1.5/1/2.5/2 are binding (docs/REVIEW-GATES-LIFECYCLE.md); evidence is per SHA; review churn is bounded (BI-PF-1480).
Backlog is the work SSOT and is written only through core.backlog (API); evidence attaches to the owner store and references item_id.
Precheck fast runs scoped tests/gates; --full/CI adds the wide set. Timings are printed but not persisted per item.
core.audit_trail.py / core.backlog.py set the precedent for Python control-plane/evidence tooling (not customer runtime).
existing_path: core/backlog.py: set_status/set_delivery/update; item decisions/evidence/verification/delivery; execution.usage from workers.
scripts/dev/gate0_check.py, architect_review.py, gate_decide.py/gate_decisions.py, precheck.py, gate2_completion_check.py, review_churn_check.py.
assumptions: A trail is a per-item append-only JSON store; stages are recorded by the tools, not hand-written.
Completion (status completed) is the enforcement point for the pre-merge stages; merge/delivery/completion events are appended after the PR/merge.

Provider usage (input/output/cached tokens) is available from the review API response; coding-session tokens are only available if the harness/worker writes item.execution.usage, otherwise shown as 'not captured'.
DEFERRED dispositions must name a follow-up item id in their note; the completion gate checks it when present.
divergences: The trail is a new evidence store (not a backlog field) to keep the item lean and the history append-only; it references item_id.
The trail is written by the gate tools (automatic) and checked at completion (fail closed), rather than relying on manual summaries.

impact_review.evidence: No HTTP surface: core CLI + gate tooling; no route/tenant input.

impact_review.evidence: Python control-plane/evidence tooling (core/execution_trail.py + scripts/dev), not customer runtime; language_rule_review will be run.
Extends the existing gate tools (gate0, architect_review, gate_decide, precheck, backlog) and reuses the evidence/decisions stores; no second backlog or review engine.
execution_trail_check in precheck fails a completion with missing/out-of-order stages or an unlinked DEFERRED; legacy items are not in the diff.
Review usage is captured; session usage is shown as not captured unless item.execution.usage exists. No fabricated cost.
Trail writes are best-effort in the tools; the completion gate is the enforcement. Rollback is a revert; trail files are append-only evidence.

verification: Objective achieved: Backlog execution trail: ordered stage ledger + tests/usage/cost report + completion guard
risks: A trail write failure must not fail a gate; the completion gate catches a missing trail.
Concurrent sessions: the trail uses a per-item lock and append-only events.
Legacy items have no trail; the gate only enforces completions in the diff.
Session token/cost may be unavailable; the report says so instead of guessing.
rollback: Revert the tooling/config commit; trail files are append-only evidence and can remain.

analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend core/audit_trail.py + core/agent_ledger.py with an ordered stage-ledger append path (monotonic seq per run); add report build on core/cost_kpi.py + artifacts API /api/v1/artifacts/{stage_id}/{agent}; completion guard via guardrail-policy.json checks before /api/v1/backlog/{id} close.
conflict_findings: BI-0001 ledger unification may edit core/agent_ledger.py concurrently
duplication_findings: BI-PF-1241 owns execution.usage rollup — reuse, do not re-capture tokens
BI-0001 unifying ledgers — stage ledger must be core-owned, not a new ledger
analysis.rationale: Reuse-first: ordering + trail lives in existing audit/agent ledgers; cost report reuses cost_kpi/usage rollup; completion guard reuses guardrail-policy — no new component needed.
assumptions: single-writer append per run into stage ledger
usage numbers sourced from BI-PF-1241 execution.usage
close-guard enforced via existing guardrail-policy config, not a new service
risks: duplicate/conflicting ledger writers if BI-0001 lands concurrently
ordering invariant break under concurrent stage appends
guard could block legitimate closes (false positive)
missing_info: which stage set/order is authoritative (canonical stage taxonomy)
whether report is per-run, per-backlog-item, or both

api_impact.reason: CLI/gate tooling only; no HTTP surface.

language_rule: Python control-plane/evidence tooling (core + scripts), not customer runtime; language_rule_review to be cited.
